title: Interleaved Capacity Viz and Decision Canvas for Cycle Negotiation
creator: Lena Ortiz
description:
Goal: Create a lightweight, reusable decision canvas and visualization that helps product managers, engineering leads, and design partners make on-the-spot staffing and scope-trim decisions during cycle planning and mid-cycle rebalancing.

Problem: Current cycle planning conversations devolve into prolonged debates because there is no single shared artifact that combines: (1) staffed capacity by role, (2) priority-aligned feature slices, (3) tradeoff impact estimates (customer value / risk / dev effort), and (4) suggested soft-freeze / surge triggers. Teams end up over-committing or leaving too much reserve unused.

Proposal: Build an "Interleaved Capacity Viz" (ICV) + Decision Canvas template with the following components:
- Role-capacity lane view: FTEs by role and timeboxed availability (including cross-functional shadowing lanes).
- Initiative heatmap: OKR / initiative slices mapped to staffed lanes with color-coded risk and value scores.
- Tranche slider: quick knobs to adjust committed scope % and show resulting velocity / delivery date deltas.
- Soft-freeze & surge rules pane: suggested actions (defer, reduce scope, open surge window) with guardrails and who to call.
- Exportable snapshot for executive review and for downstream engineering capacity allocation.

Deliverables:
1) Interactive Figma template + static Confluence playbook with step-by-step facilitator script.
2) One-page PDF decision canvas for readouts.
3) Minimal MVP web view (internal tooling) that reads current headcount and cycle commitments from the Capacity Ledger (read-only) and renders scenario diffs.

Success metrics:
- Reduce median cycle-planning meeting time by 30% for involved teams.
- Reduce mid-cycle unplanned scope shuffles (tracked as emergency scope changes) by 20% in Q2.
- Adoption: at least 6 teams use the template in the first two cycles.

Notes on approach and tradeoffs:
- Keep the MVP low-friction: initial implementation is a Figma + Confluence runbook. Web view only if Figma adoption shows persistent pain.
- Avoid automating cuts: the canvas should suggest options and highlight impacts; final decisions remain human.
- For sensitive org-level staffing numbers, the export should redact PII and salary fields.

Links & artifacts:
- Draft Figma template: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/ICV-Template (internal)
- Confluence playbook draft: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PM/pages/987654321/Interleaved+Capacity+Viz+Playbook
- Capacity Ledger readme: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1X_capacity_ledger_readme
- Capacity dashboard for scenario data: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/capacity-simulator

Open questions: 
1) Should we include cost estimates (dollars) in the initial canvas or defer to Optimize team? Recommendation: defer to Optimize for dollarized outputs; include relative effort multipliers in MVP.
2) What permission model for the web view? Default to view-only for non-leads; editing limited to PMs and Eng leads.
3) Which teams will pilot? Recommend infra, console, and runtime PMs.
